cover: Write a software brief a developer can price

slides.title: Start with the problem
slides.body: Say what goes wrong today and what it costs. That tells a developer more than naming the system you think you need.

slides.title: List each user and their job
slides.body: "A driver marks each job done from a phone" is a piece of work someone can estimate.

slides.title: Attach the real spreadsheet
slides.body: Keep the columns and the messy parts. A developer learns more from your actual sheet than from a description of it.

slides.title: Name every system it touches
slides.body: Accounting, CRM, online store. Integrations are where estimates most often go wrong.

slides.title: Give a budget range and a date
slides.body: With a range, developers can tell you what fits inside it. With the reason for the date, they can plan a smaller first release.

slides.title: Mark what can wait
slides.body: Split features into needed at launch and useful later. That list controls the price more than anything else.
